prompt: He changed five things at once; it works now, but he doesn't know which fix did it.
why: Change one thing at a time so you know what helped.
trap: It's not about the latest change; it's about many at once.

prompt: She tries one fix, tests, undoes it, then tries the next.
tells: tries one fix, tests, undoes it
why: Testing each change alone shows its effect.
trap: It isn't halving; it's single changes.

prompt: Several tweaks fixed the bug but caused a new one, and no one knows which tweak did it.
tells: no one knows which tweak did it
why: Mixing changes hides which one caused what.
trap: Looking at changes is needed because they weren't made one by one.

prompt: He commits after each small fix so he can go back to any step.
why: Small steps keep each change separate.
trap: It helps track changes, but the habit is one at a time.

prompt: Instead of changing every setting, she changes one and checks again.
why: One change per test keeps cause and effect clear.
trap: It's settings, but the method is one at a time.

prompt: Randomly tweaking code until it works left a mess nobody understands.
tells: Randomly tweaking code until it works
why: Changing many things blindly is the opposite of one change at a time.
trap: Fixing the cause is the goal; the mistake was scattershot changes.
